To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ATLAS system is a powerful database language, which is Turing-complete, yet it is very simple to use, and that the ATLAS SQL language is a very good candidate to be the next standard database language.

(1) SQL is a powerful database language that is Turing-complete and is suitable for advanced data-intensive applications; (2) ATLAS' SQL can be used to implement data mining and stream processing algorithms, and can be used to develop complete applications; and (3) ATLAS' internal design is modular, and is composed of three key modules, namely, a rewrite module, a query-plan generation module and a stream-data management engine.
• ATLAS' SQL enables users to develop complex data-intensive applications in SQL, without resorting to procedural languages, and with a small performance overhead.
In summary, our research is concerned with
extending the capabilities of SQL to enable it to be used as a complete programming language for developing data-intensive applications.
developing a database system that is suitable for data mining applications and for stream queries.
extending the SQL language to support data-intensive applications such as stream queries and data mining, while retaining the simplicity of SQL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATLAS is a powerful database system for data mining and stream processing.
ATLAS is the first SQL-based system that enables users of relational databases and Object-Relational DBMSs (ORDBMSs) to write data mining and stream applications in SQL.

the ATLAS project has demonstrated that SQL, as it stands, is a very suitable and efficient language for implementing complex data-intensive applications, and that it is not necessary to use a separate procedural language for this purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATLAS' SQL provides a very simple and powerful extension to SQL that enables users to write complex data-intensive applications, and that ATLAS' architecture is simple and efficient.
the design and implementation of ATLAS is a significant step toward the goal of making the SQL language complete, and thus suitable for a wide variety of data-intensive applications.
the SQL language has been extended with a small but complete set of constructs that enable users to write advanced data mining and stream applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SQL can indeed be used as a programming language for data mining and stream processing.
it is now possible for users to write data-intensive applications in SQL, rather then in C/C++, which is a major step forward in the usability of data-intensive systems.
it is possible to implement a powerful and efficient data management system in SQL, without resorting to procedural languages or other non-SQL extensions.
